# FIELDSTEP

## Site
- Site area: 9,600 m².
- Boundary: rectangle, 120 m east–west × 80 m south–north.
- Coordinate origin: southwest corner; x east, y north; coordinates in m.
- Elevation datum: local project datum, in m.
- Terrace levels: 100.00, 102.00, 104.00 and 106.00 m.
- Total rise: 6.00 m.
- Route arrangement: eastern out-and-back route, southern entrance, northern turnaround.

## Zones
| Name | Area | Existing or proposed surfaces | Shade | Occupancy |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Working Terraces | 8,640 m² | Existing rice soil, stone-faced risers, compacted-stone production lane | Open agricultural ground | 12 farmers |
| Visitor Edge | 960 m² | Compacted crushed-stone level paths; textured timber node decks | One removable textile shade structure per node | 18 visitors across three nodes |

## Agricultural infrastructure
- Production corridor: x = 0–8 m.
- Production lane: x = 2–6 m; clear width 4,000 mm.
- Irrigation channel: x = 104–105 m; open width 1,000 mm; depth 400 mm below adjacent terrace level.
- Channel maintenance corridor: x = 102–107 m; total width 5,000 mm, including channel.
- Existing drop structures: D1, D2, D3.
- Field identifiers: R1, R2, R3, R4.
- Existing stonework: irregular gray stone faces and stone-lined irrigation structures.

## Observation nodes
| Name | Center x | Center y | Envelope | Adjacent terrace level | Occupancy |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Lower Lookout | 116 m | 10 m | 4,000 × 4,000 mm | 100.00 m | 6 visitors |
| Water Lookout | 116 m | 30 m | 4,000 × 4,000 mm | 102.00 m | 6 visitors |
| Upper Lookout | 116 m | 70 m | 4,000 × 4,000 mm | 106.00 m | 6 visitors |

## Material palette
- Level walking surfaces: compacted crushed stone.
- Observation decks: textured timber boards.
- Node shade: removable textile structures.
- Existing terrace faces: irregular gray stone.

## Existing plants
| Code | Name | Location |
|---|---|---|
| OS | Oryza sativa | Fields R1–R4 |
| JE | Juncus effusus | Eastern channel margin |
| PH | Persicaria hydropiper | Western channel margin |

## Printed wording
- Site name: FIELDSTEP.
- Entrance phrase: Fields at work.
- Zone names: Working Terraces; Visitor Edge.
- Node names: Lower Lookout; Water Lookout; Upper Lookout.

## Seasonal states
- Irrigation season: shallow standing water, young rice and farmers tending water distribution.
- Harvest season: mature golden rice, cut patches and farmers carrying harvested bundles.
- Upper Lookout seasonal pair: identical camera, node geometry and framing.

steps.userMessage:
FIELDSTEP | A walking route through working rice terraces

Our farming cooperative is opening a short walking route beside four working rice terraces. FIELDSTEP occupies a rectangular 9,600 m² site, 120 m east to west and 80 m south to north. The direction is fixed: an out-and-back visitor route in the eastern strip, with three small observation nodes. The terraces, stone-faced risers, irrigation channel and western production lane remain in use throughout the project.

Working Terraces occupies 8,640 m²; Visitor Edge occupies 960 m² and is 12 m wide. Ground rises from elevation 100.00 m at the southern entrance to 106.00 m at the northern end, through terrace levels of 100.00, 102.00, 104.00 and 106.00 m. The existing production lane has a 4,000 mm clear width. The irrigation channel is 1,000 mm wide and 400 mm deep, with three existing drop structures and a 5,000 mm maintenance corridor. Visitor Edge contains three 4,000 × 4,000 mm node envelopes, centered at the coordinates in the site records, each accommodating six visitors. Use compacted crushed stone for level walking surfaces, textured timber for node decks and removable textile shade at the nodes. The existing plants are Oryza sativa, Juncus effusus and Persicaria hydropiper. Print the site name as "FIELDSTEP" on the masterplan, entrance panel and presentation cover; the entrance panel also carries "Fields at work".

Audience: terrace visitors and local farmers, with the cooperative using the work to agree the route, agricultural access and locations for visitor stops.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the site facts, zone areas, material palette and plant names. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md contains the deliverable proportions, formats and stages. 03-site-records.en.md contains coordinates, terrace levels, protected corridors, node envelopes and view positions. terrace-base-plan.png provides the fixed boundary, level lines, field numbers, irrigation infrastructure and production access. terrace-long-section.png provides the existing ground profile through the three node envelopes. irrigation-cross-section.png provides the existing channel and maintenance corridor at the middle terrace. existing-terraces.png establishes the appearance of the working fields, stone-faced risers and irrigation structures. irrigation-season.png provides the flooded-field season and the relationship between farmers and visitors. harvest-season.png provides the same landscape in harvest season.

Deliverables:
1. A two-page site analysis and specification with the two-zone area table, surface materials, shade provision, occupancy, three plant names and route-level sequence
2. One masterplan with visitor and production routes, four numbered fields, three node envelopes, irrigation infrastructure, plant codes, section lines, view positions, north arrow, scale bar and site boundary
3. One longitudinal section A–A through all three observation nodes, with existing and proposed levels, walking connections and stair dimensions
4. One cross-section B–B through the middle node and irrigation channel, with channel dimensions, maintenance clearance and deck supports
5. Three node detail sheets, one each for Lower Lookout, Water Lookout and Upper Lookout, with a plan, section, seating and removable shade
6. One materials and planting schedule with the site name, both zone names and areas, three plant names and codes, and the crushed-stone, timber and textile specifications
7. One interpretation and wayfinding sheet containing an entrance panel, a water-management panel and three node markers, with their locations and printed wording
8. Three walking perspectives: the southern approach in irrigation season, Upper Lookout in irrigation season and Upper Lookout in harvest season
9. One 10-second route video moving from the southern entrance through the three nodes to the northern end
10. One presentation document of at least 10 pages, reusing the specification, masterplan, sections, node details, schedule, signage and seasonal perspectives

Acceptance:
- Repeat Working Terraces, 8,640 m², Visitor Edge and 960 m² from the site analysis on the masterplan, materials and planting schedule and presentation; repeat Oryza sativa, Juncus effusus and Persicaria hydropiper with codes OS, JE and PH on those same deliverables.
- Show the 120 m × 80 m boundary on the masterplan; retain fields R1–R4, the 4,000 mm production-lane clearance, the 1,000 mm channel, drop structures D1–D3 and the 5,000 mm maintenance corridor. Place the visitor route and all three nodes within Visitor Edge.
- Match sections A–A and B–B to their recorded cuts. Carry elevations 100.00, 102.00, 104.00 and 106.00 m through A–A; dimension each proposed stair flight. Show the 400 mm channel depth and the full maintenance corridor on B–B, with node supports inside the recorded node envelope.
- Locate the three node detail sheets at their recorded centers, each within 4,000 × 4,000 mm and accommodating six visitors. Repeat their textured timber decks and removable textile shade in the masterplan, materials and planting schedule, walking perspectives and presentation.
- Print FIELDSTEP on the masterplan, entrance panel and presentation cover, and Fields at work on the entrance panel. Use Lower Lookout, Water Lookout and Upper Lookout on the three node markers, corresponding node details and masterplan.
- Use the recorded cameras for the three walking perspectives, with the two Upper Lookout views sharing geometry and framing across irrigation and harvest seasons. Follow the entrance–Lower Lookout–Water Lookout–Upper Lookout–northern end sequence in the 10-second video, and reuse both seasonal Upper Lookout views in the presentation of at least 10 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
